note: Adapted from Emerson's (1928) species-level description; the original is in English and covers only the major and minor soldiers, with no worker or alate. The same treatment also includes a description of the subspecies sulciceps, which does not belong to this species and is not included; figure numbers, localities and field records are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Distinguished from the subspecies sulciceps by the absence of a longitudinal groove behind the head and the shorter nasus; N. ruficeps and the form kalaharicus of N. gemellus are smaller. After carefully comparing this species with the syntypes of N. brutus, Emerson considered the two names synonyms, since the size difference is visible within a single colony and the anterior margin of the pronotum of the small soldier syntypes shows no difference either.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier: head red-yellow; concave in lateral view; antennal base situated before the middle of the head; no longitudinal groove behind the head. Antennae 13-segmented, the third segment usually twice as long as the fourth; sometimes the fourth segment is incompletely separated, sometimes almost as long as the third. Nasus proportionally shorter than in the subspecies sulciceps and thicker. Anterior margin of the pronotum with a distinct notch. Head length 2.33–2.58 mm; head width 1.40–1.44 mm; pronotum length 0.28 mm, width 0.67 mm; length of the hind tibia 1.44 mm. Minor soldier: antennae 12-segmented, the third segment about as long as the fourth, the second smaller. Anterior margin of the pronotum with a distinct notch. Head length 1.67–1.78 mm; head width 0.72–0.84 mm; length of the hind tibia 1.27–1.38 mm.
